newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - Buba exempts securities from reserves.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Buba exempts securities from reserves.

text.p: Following are comments from analysts on the Bundesbank's decision on Thursday to exempt certain securities repurchase business from minimum reserve requirements from January 1, 1997 in a widely-expected step designed to enhance Germany's stature as a financial centre.

JUERGEN PFISTER, SENIOR ECONOMIST COMMERZBANK: "I think its an important sign from the Bundesbank. Germany is under severe international pressure. The Bundesbank has created a level playing field. The quantitative impact on banks will not be large. The intital impact will only be very small."
"A lot of this business already takes place outside Germany. Over the next 12 to 18 months, business will start to move back to Germany."
Dr Hermann Remsperger, chief economist, BHF Bank
"The most important aspect of this move to free the repo from minimum reserves is that such a measure boosts the financial centre of Frankfurt without harming monetary policy.
This means that minimum reserves can continue to carry out their function but there has been a crucial freeing-up process.
I think this is also one of the more pleasant effects of the run-up to currency union."
